about: The Lab's core-medicine course, in teaching order. The daily pipeline builds the first module that is neither shipped (in lab/apps.json) nor withdrawn (in lab/rejected.json). Reorder, add or remove modules by editing this list; never change the slug of a shipped lesson. drugClasses are the drug classes and disease states each lesson animates (never doses). Units group the modules; a module's unit is one of the ids in units, and modules of one unit sit together.

units.title: The heart, the kidney and blood pressure
units.summary: How the heart fills and pumps, how the kidney handles salt and water, and the reflexes and hormones that hold blood pressure steady.

units.title: Nerves, rhythm and muscle
units.summary: How nerves pass a signal on to organs and muscle, and the ion currents that set the rhythm of the heart.

units.title: Breath and blood
units.summary: How blood carries oxygen, how the lung matches air to blood, how blood pH is held steady, and how a clot is built.

units.title: Hormones
units.summary: Three hormone systems that run on feedback: insulin and glucose, the thyroid, and cortisol.

units.title: The gut and drug handling
units.summary: How the stomach makes acid on command, and how any drug's level rises and falls in the blood.

units.title: Inflammation, infection, immunity and cancer
units.summary: How the body raises inflammation, fights bacteria, mounts an immune response and keeps cell division in check, and the drugs that act at each point.

units.title: Water and calcium balance
units.summary: How antidiuretic hormone sets how much water the kidney keeps, and how parathyroid hormone and vitamin D move calcium among the gut, bone and kidney.

units.title: Lung volumes
units.summary: How a forced breath is measured, which air a spirometer can see, and how obstruction and restriction change the curves.

units.title: Cells, membranes and signals
units.summary: How water and ions cross a membrane, how a nerve fires and a receptor answers, and what a cell does when oxygen runs short or the cell is injured.

units.title: Heart and vessels
units.summary: The cardiac cycle and the valves, coronary flow, failure and rhythm, and the circulation in shock and before birth.

units.title: Kidney, fluids and electrolytes
units.summary: How the kidney filters, reabsorbs and clears, and the sodium, potassium and acid problems that follow when a segment, or the whole kidney, fails.

modules.title: The Pressure–Volume Loop
modules.description: How one heartbeat fills and empties the left ventricle, drawn as a loop, and how fluids, blood pressure and heart drugs reshape it.
drugClasses: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

modules.title: The Nephron and Diuretics
modules.description: Follow salt and water along a nephron, segment by segment, and see where each diuretic blocks salt reabsorption and how much water follows it out.
modules.notes: Loop diuretic step: show Na+ leaving the nephron in the urine and blood volume dropping.

modules.title: Frank–Starling and Cardiac Output
modules.description: Why a fuller heart pumps harder, and how filling, heart rate and contraction strength add up to cardiac output.

modules.title: Blood Pressure Regulation
modules.description: Blood pressure as flow times resistance, and how the baroreflex keeps it steady from one moment to the next.

modules.title: The Renin–Angiotensin–Aldosterone System
modules.description: The hormone chain the kidney uses to raise blood pressure and hold on to salt, and the drugs that cut it at each link.

modules.title: The Autonomic Synapse
modules.description: How sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves talk to organs through receptors, and how drugs mimic or block that signal.

modules.title: The Cardiac Action Potential
modules.description: The ion currents behind each heartbeat, in pacemaker and muscle cells, and how antiarrhythmic drugs change their shape.

modules.title: The Neuromuscular Junction
modules.description: How a nerve signal becomes a muscle contraction, and how paralytic and reversal drugs act at the junction.

modules.title: Oxygen and Hemoglobin
modules.description: Why hemoglobin grabs oxygen in the lungs and lets go in the tissues, drawn as the dissociation curve, and what shifts it.

modules.title: Ventilation, Perfusion and the Alveolus
modules.description: How air and blood meet in the lung, and what happens to oxygen when the two are mismatched.

modules.title: Acid–Base Balance
modules.description: The bicarbonate buffer, the lungs and the kidneys working together to hold blood pH steady, and the four ways it goes wrong.

modules.title: The Coagulation Cascade
modules.description: How a clot is built, from platelet plug to fibrin mesh, and where each anticoagulant and clot-busting drug acts.

modules.title: Insulin and Glucose
modules.description: How insulin moves glucose out of the blood after a meal, what fails in diabetes, and how each diabetes drug helps.

modules.title: The Thyroid Axis
modules.description: The brain-to-thyroid feedback loop that sets the body's metabolic pace, and the drugs that replace or suppress thyroid hormone.

modules.title: The HPA Axis and Steroids
modules.description: How the brain and adrenal glands control cortisol through feedback, and why steroid drugs switch the axis off.

modules.title: Stomach Acid and the Parietal Cell
modules.description: How one stomach cell pumps acid on command, and how acid-reducing drugs turn it down at different steps.

modules.title: Pharmacokinetics: Drug Levels Over Time
modules.description: How a drug's level rises, plateaus and falls in the blood: absorption, distribution, half-life and steady state, drawn as curves.

modules.title: Inflammation and the Arachidonic Acid Pathway
modules.description: How injured cells make prostaglandins and leukotrienes, and where anti-inflammatory drugs block the pathway.

modules.title: The Bacterial Cell and Antibiotic Targets
modules.description: A tour of a bacterium's wall, ribosomes and DNA machinery, and the antibiotic families that attack each one.

modules.title: The Immune Response
modules.description: How the body recognises an invader, from the first innate response to antibodies and memory, and how immune drugs steer it.

modules.title: The Cell Cycle and Chemotherapy
modules.description: How a cell copies itself, phase by phase, and which chemotherapy drugs strike at which phase.

modules.title: ADH and Water Balance
modules.description: Watch the brain sense blood saltiness, release ADH and open water channels in the kidney, then see urine change in DI, SIADH and polydipsia.
drugClasses: Water deficit (blood more concentrated, ADH rises)
Water excess (blood more dilute, ADH falls)
Central diabetes insipidus (too little ADH made)
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (the kidney ignores ADH)
SIADH (ADH that will not switch off)
modules.notes: Owns the ADH loop and its breaks: water deficit, water excess, central and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, SIADH and primary polydipsia. Hyponatremia sorting and osmotic demyelination belong to hyponatremia-osmotic-demyelination.

modules.title: Calcium, PTH and Vitamin D
modules.description: Follow PTH from the parathyroid to bone and kidney, then calcitriol to the gut, and see calcium shift in four parathyroid, vitamin D and kidney states.
drugClasses: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PTH that ignores the calcium)
Vitamin D deficiency (the gut absorbs less calcium)
Decreased renal function (phosphate retained, less calcitriol made)

modules.title: Spirometry and Lung Volumes
modules.description: Blow out a model breath and watch the spirogram, flow–volume loop and lung-volume bars redraw in asthma, emphysema, fibrosis and after a bronchodilator.
drugClasses: Emphysema (obstruction, the lung stretches more easily)
Poor effort (the curves fall without establishing disease)
modules.notes: The spirogram, the flow-volume loop and the volume bars. oxygen-hemoglobin-dissociation owns gas carriage and ventilation-perfusion owns matching air to blood. Do not rebuild those. Obstruction and restriction here are patterns on these curves, not a second lesson on either of those.

modules.title: Diffusion, Osmosis and IV Fluids
modules.description: How water and a dissolved substance cross a membrane, and why the tonicity of an intravenous fluid decides whether a cell swells, shrinks or holds its size.
drugClasses: Free water, including a glucose solution once the sugar is taken up

modules.title: The Na⁺/K⁺ Pump (digoxin)
modules.description: The pump that keeps sodium outside the cell and potassium inside, and how digoxin slows that pump so the heart cell holds more calcium and squeezes harder.
drugClasses: Hypokalemia (digoxin binds the pump more readily)
Hyperkalemia (digoxin binds the pump less readily)

modules.title: Resting Membrane Potential and Potassium
modules.description: Why a resting cell is negative inside, and how the potassium outside the cell moves that voltage toward or away from the point where it fires.
drugClasses: Resting potential as a potassium diffusion potential
Sodium-channel inactivation when the membrane stays depolarized

modules.title: Nerve Action Potential and Local Anesthetics
modules.description: The sodium rush that carries an impulse along a nerve, and how a local anesthetic binds the sodium channel and stops the impulse.
drugClasses: Use-dependent block of open and inactivated channels
Acidic tissue (more of the drug stays charged outside the nerve)

modules.title: Myelin and Conduction Velocity (MS, GBS)
modules.description: How myelin lets an impulse jump from node to node, and how that jump fails when myelin is lost in the brain and spinal cord or in a peripheral nerve.

modules.title: Ion Channels and Channelopathies (CFTR, congenital long QT)
modules.description: A channel as a gated pore, told through two broken pores: chloride that cannot leave the airway, and a heart muscle cell that cannot finish repolarizing.
drugClasses: CFTR failure (chloride cannot leave the airway)
Congenital long QT from loss of a repolarizing potassium current
A sodium channel that fails to inactivate
modules.notes: The channel, with CFTR and a congenital long-QT current as the examples. long-qt-torsades owns the ECG, the pause and drug-induced torsades. Do not draw torsades here.

modules.title: GPCRs and Second Messengers (cholera and pertussis toxin)
modules.description: How a receptor on the cell surface turns a signal into a second messenger inside, and how cholera toxin and pertussis toxin lock a G protein on or off.
drugClasses: Gq (IP3 and a rise in cell calcium)

modules.title: Dose–Response: Agonists, Antagonists and Partial Agonists
modules.description: How occupying more of a receptor gives a larger effect, up to a ceiling, and how a full agonist, a partial agonist and an antagonist each move that curve.
drugClasses: Competitive antagonists (the curve shifts right, the ceiling holds)

modules.title: Enzyme Kinetics and Inhibitors
modules.description: How an enzyme's speed rises with its substrate and then levels off, and how a competitive inhibitor and a noncompetitive inhibitor bend that curve differently.
drugClasses: Competitive inhibitors (same ceiling, more substrate needed)

modules.title: Oxidative Phosphorylation
modules.description: How the electron transport chain stores energy as a proton gradient and ATP synthase spends it, and what fails when the chain, the gradient or the oxygen at the end is blocked.
drugClasses: Uncouplers (the proton gradient spent as heat)
No oxygen as the final acceptor
modules.notes: Carbon monoxide here blocks complex IV. oxygen-hemoglobin-dissociation already owns carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin. Do not redraw that curve.

modules.title: Glycolysis, Lactate and Lactic Acidosis
modules.description: How glucose is split to pyruvate, when pyruvate is turned to lactate instead of entering the mitochondrion, and why lactate then rises in the blood.
drugClasses: Metformin when lactate cannot be cleared

modules.title: Cell Adaptation
modules.description: How a cell grows, shrinks, multiplies or changes its type when the demand on it changes, and what each of those looks like in an organ.

modules.title: Cell Injury, Necrosis and Apoptosis
modules.description: Where reversible injury ends, and how necrosis and apoptosis take a cell apart in different ways.

modules.title: Hypoxia and the Ischemic Cascade
modules.description: What a cell does in the minutes after its blood flow stops: ATP falls, sodium and calcium come in, and the membrane fails.

modules.title: Starling Forces and Edema
modules.description: The four forces that decide whether fluid stays in a capillary or leaves it, and the ways that balance tips into edema.

modules.title: The Cardiac Cycle in Time
modules.description: One heartbeat drawn against time: atrial, ventricular and aortic pressure, ventricular volume, and the moments the valves open and shut.
drugClasses: A shorter diastole at a faster rate
modules.notes: The time plot of one beat. pressure-volume-loop already owns the loop and how drugs reshape it. Keep this lesson to timing, the valve events and the pressure curves.

modules.title: Heart Sounds and Murmurs
modules.description: Where the first and second heart sounds come from, and how the timing and shape of a murmur, and where it is loudest, point to a valve.
drugClasses: High flow across a normal valve
A change in preload or afterload (the murmur louder or softer)
modules.notes: How a sound is made and how a murmur is described. The four valve lessons own aortic stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis and aortic regurgitation. Do not reteach each lesion here.

modules.title: Aortic Stenosis
modules.description: A narrowed aortic valve the left ventricle must force blood through, the slow-rising pulse that follows, and why the ventricle thickens and can then fail.
drugClasses: Arterial vasodilation (output cannot rise, coronary perfusion falls)

modules.title: Mitral Regurgitation
modules.description: A mitral valve that leaks into the atrium while the ventricle is ejecting, so part of each stroke goes backward and the atrium and ventricle enlarge.
drugClasses: Arterial vasodilation (more forward flow, less backward)
Acute regurgitation into an atrium that has not enlarged

modules.title: Mitral Stenosis
modules.description: A narrowed mitral valve that holds blood in the left atrium, raises pressure back into the lungs, and leaves the left ventricle underfilled.
drugClasses: A faster rate (less time for diastolic filling)

modules.title: Aortic Regurgitation
modules.description: An aortic valve that leaks back into the ventricle during diastole, so the ventricle fills from two directions and the pulse pressure widens.
drugClasses: Acute regurgitation into a ventricle that has not enlarged
A slower rate (a longer diastole, more leak)

modules.title: Coronary Flow and Oxygen Demand
modules.description: Why heart muscle receives its blood in diastole, what raises its need for oxygen, and how nitrates, beta-blockers and calcium channel blockers change the demand or the supply.
drugClasses: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (coronary and arterial dilation)
Non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (slower rate, less contractility)
A faster rate (less time for coronary flow in diastole)

modules.title: Atherosclerosis and Plaque Rupture
modules.description: How a plaque grows inside an artery wall, what tears its cap, and how that tear becomes a clot that narrows or blocks the lumen.
drugClasses: A vulnerable plaque (thin cap, large lipid core)

modules.title: Acute Coronary Syndromes and Troponin
modules.description: How a coronary clot shows up as unstable angina or as an infarction with or without ST elevation, and why troponin rises only after muscle has died.

modules.title: Heart Failure: The Neurohormonal Spiral
modules.description: How a weak left ventricle turns on sympathetic drive, the renin axis and antidiuretic hormone, and how those same responses then make the failure worse.
drugClasses: Neurohormonal activation (sympathetic drive, the renin axis, antidiuretic hormone)
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers
ARNIs (neprilysin inhibition plus angiotensin receptor block)
modules.notes: The spiral, and the drugs that interrupt it. renin-angiotensin-aldosterone already owns the axis itself. Loop diuretics lower the congestion and do not stop the spiral.

modules.title: Diastolic Dysfunction and HFpEF
modules.description: A ventricle that still ejects a normal share of its volume but fills stiffly, so pressure rises and the lungs flood while the ejection fraction looks preserved.
drugClasses: A stiff ventricle with a preserved ejection fraction

modules.title: Cardiomyopathies
modules.description: Three diseases of the muscle itself: one that dilates and weakens, one that thickens and can obstruct outflow, and one that only stiffens.

modules.title: Tamponade and Pulsus Paradoxus
modules.description: Fluid under pressure in the pericardial sac, the diastolic pressures that come together, and the fall in systolic pressure that a deep breath produces.

modules.title: The ECG: Vectors to Waves
modules.description: How the heart's electrical vector, read from the limb and chest leads, becomes the P wave, the QRS complex and the T wave.
drugClasses: The P wave as the atrial vector
The QRS as the ventricular vector
A lead as a viewpoint on that vector
modules.notes: Mechanism only: how a vector becomes a wave. Not a strip trainer, and distinct from the site's EKG trainer (Read This, at /ekg/). Do not drill rhythm names or ask the reader to call a tracing.

modules.title: The Conduction System and Heart Block
modules.description: The path of an impulse from the sinus node to the ventricular muscle, and what the rhythm does when that path delays or blocks.
drugClasses: Beta-blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (slower nodal conduction)
modules.notes: The wiring and the blocks. ecg-vectors-to-waves owns how a vector becomes a wave. Do not reteach the leads here.

modules.title: Atrial Fibrillation: Rate, Rhythm and Stroke
modules.description: Atria that quiver instead of contracting, a ventricular rate set by how many impulses cross the AV node, and clot forming in the atrial appendage.
drugClasses: Rate control at the AV node (beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers)
Rhythm control (class Ic and class III antiarrhythmics)
Stasis and thrombus in the appendage

modules.title: Reentry and Ventricular Tachycardia
modules.description: A circuit that runs around a scar or a split pathway and keeps restarting itself, and how an impulse that enters the circuit at the right moment can stop it.
drugClasses: A circuit that can be entered and extinguished
Sodium channel blockers (conduction in the circuit slows)

modules.title: Long QT and Torsades
modules.description: A ventricular action potential that takes too long to finish, the early afterdepolarization that follows a pause, and the twisting tachycardia that comes next.
drugClasses: Repolarizing potassium current blocked (class III and other QT-prolonging drugs)
A pause, then an early afterdepolarization
modules.notes: The rhythm: a long QT, a pause and torsades. ion-channels-channelopathies owns the channel itself, including congenital long QT as a broken repolarizing current. Do not reteach channel structure here.

modules.title: Shock: Four Kinds on One Picture
modules.description: The same failure of perfusion drawn four ways: too little volume, a pump that cannot eject, vessels that have opened too wide, and a flow that is obstructed.
modules.notes: Four patterns on one picture. tamponade-pulsus-paradoxus owns the pericardial constraint and the paradox. Obstructive shock here is one of the four, not a second tamponade lesson.

modules.title: Vasopressors and Inotropes at the Receptor
modules.description: Which receptor each vasopressor and inotrope acts on, and what that does to heart rate, the strength of the squeeze, and the vessels.
modules.notes: One step per receptor effect. Do not draw an infusion-rate ladder, and do not sort dopamine by how fast it is run.

modules.title: Pulmonary Hypertension and the Right Heart
modules.description: A right ventricle pumping into a high-pressure lung circuit, and the three places that pressure can come from: the lung arteries, the left heart, or low oxygen.
drugClasses: Pressure passed back from the left heart

modules.title: Fetal Circulation and Congenital Shunts
modules.description: How blood bypasses the lungs before birth, what closes those bypasses with the first breaths, and how a hole between the two circuits sends blood the wrong way.
drugClasses: Ductus venosus, foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus open
The first breaths (pulmonary resistance falls and the bypasses close)
Left-to-right shunt (septal defects, a patent ductus)
Right-to-left shunt once right-sided pressure exceeds left

modules.title: Glomerular Filtration and GFR
modules.description: How pressure in the glomerular capillary pushes a protein-free filtrate into Bowman's space, and which way the arterioles have to change for that filtration to rise or fall.
drugClasses: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (efferent dilation, filtration falls)

modules.title: Clearance and Creatinine
modules.description: Clearance as the volume of plasma completely freed of a substance each minute, and why the creatinine in the blood rises only after a large share of filtration is already gone.
drugClasses: Inulin (filtered only, the measure of GFR)
PAH (filtered and secreted, a measure of renal plasma flow)
A late rise in blood creatinine as GFR falls
Drugs that block creatinine secretion (the blood level rises, filtration unchanged)

modules.title: Autoregulation and Tubuloglomerular Feedback
modules.description: How the kidney holds filtration nearly steady as arterial pressure changes, by afferent tone and by the macula densa tasting the salt leaving the thick limb.
drugClasses: A rise in arterial pressure (afferent constriction)
A fall in arterial pressure (afferent dilation)
Tubuloglomerular feedback (more salt at the macula densa, afferent constriction)
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers when renal flow is already low

modules.title: The Proximal Tubule and SGLT2 Inhibitors
modules.description: The first segment of the nephron, which takes back most of the filtered sodium, bicarbonate and glucose, and what stays in the tubule when the glucose transporter is blocked.
drugClasses: SGLT2 inhibitors (glucose stays in the tubule)
Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (bicarbonate stays in the tubule)
Fanconi syndrome (proximal reclaim fails across the board)
Volume contraction from proximal sodium loss
modules.notes: This segment, and the glucose that stays in the tubule. nephron-diuretics already maps every diuretic class along the whole nephron. Do not redraw that map.

modules.title: The Countercurrent Multiplier
modules.description: How the loop of Henle and the vasa recta lay down a salty medulla, and why urine can be concentrated only while that gradient is there.
drugClasses: The salt pump of the thick ascending limb
Loop diuretics (that pump stops, the gradient collapses)
The vasa recta (the gradient washed out, or held)
Antidiuretic hormone spending the gradient at the collecting duct
modules.notes: Build the medullary gradient. adh-water-balance owns ADH, the water channels and the clinical water states: here ADH only spends a gradient this lesson has built. nephron-diuretics owns the diuretic map; the loop diuretic appears only as the pump that makes the gradient.

modules.title: Renal Potassium Handling
modules.description: Potassium filtered and mostly reclaimed, then secreted again by the collecting duct under aldosterone, and the common ways that secretion runs too high or too low.
drugClasses: Loop and thiazide diuretics (more sodium arrives downstream, more secretion)
A low distal sodium delivery (less secretion)
Insulin and beta-2 agonists (potassium shifted into cells, not lost in the urine)

modules.title: Hyponatremia and Osmotic Demyelination
modules.description: How a low sodium is sorted by the concentration of the blood and of the urine, and why raising that sodium too quickly strips myelin.
drugClasses: SIADH (euvolemia, urine more concentrated than the blood)
Hypertonic hyponatremia (another solute, such as glucose, holds water in the blood)
Correction that is too fast (osmotic demyelination)
Vaptans (the collecting duct ignores antidiuretic hormone)
modules.notes: Complement adh-water-balance. Do not repeat it. That lesson owns the ADH loop, diabetes insipidus, SIADH as a broken loop, and primary polydipsia. This lesson owns how a low sodium is sorted, and the myelin injury when it is corrected too fast. SIADH is one box in that sorting, not a second ADH lesson.

modules.title: Renal Tubular Acidosis
modules.description: Three ways the tubule fails to reclaim bicarbonate or to excrete acid, and how the potassium and the urine's acidity tell them apart.
drugClasses: Distal renal tubular acidosis (the urine cannot be acidified, potassium is low)
Proximal renal tubular acidosis (bicarbonate is wasted)
Hyperkalemic renal tubular acidosis (too little aldosterone effect)

modules.title: Acute Kidney Injury: Prerenal, Intrinsic and Postrenal
modules.description: A sudden fall in filtration sorted by where it broke: too little blood arriving, the kidney tissue itself injured, or the urine blocked on the way out.
drugClasses: Prerenal azotemia (low flow, tubules still working)
The urine sodium and the sediment that separate them

modules.title: Nephrotoxic Drugs
modules.description: Drugs that injure the kidney at a named place, the arteriole, the tubule, the interstitium or the filter, each with its own picture.
drugClasses: ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (efferent dilation when flow is low)
Beta-lactams and other drugs that cause interstitial nephritis

modules.title: Chronic Kidney Disease and Its Complications
modules.description: Filtration lost for good, and what follows: phosphate, potassium, acid, salt and water retained, plus anemia and bone disease.
modules.notes: The consequences of filtration that is gone. calcium-pth-vitamin-d already owns PTH, vitamin D and decreased renal function as one of its four states. Name the bone disease here as one consequence among the others, and do not rebuild that lesson.

modules.title: Nephrotic versus Nephritic
modules.description: Two glomerular pictures: one that leaks protein until the oncotic pressure falls, and one that inflames the filter, spills blood and cuts filtration.
drugClasses: Nephritic syndrome (blood and casts in the urine, filtration falls)
Minimal change and membranous nephropathy as protein-leak states
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers (less pressure across a leaking filter)

modules.title: Dialysis
modules.description: How diffusion across a membrane clears urea, potassium and acid from the blood, and how a pressure difference pulls water off when the kidney no longer can.
drugClasses: Ultrafiltration (water pulled by a pressure difference)
Disequilibrium when solute leaves the blood faster than it leaves the brain

modules.title: Kidney Stones
modules.description: How a salt dissolved in the urine comes out of solution, and how citrate, calcium, oxalate, acidity and volume each favor a different stone.
drugClasses: Uric acid stones in acid urine
Struvite stones in infected, alkaline urine

modules.title: The Bladder and Micturition
modules.description: How the detrusor and the sphincters trade jobs to store urine and then to empty it, and how antimuscarinic and beta-3 drugs tip that trade toward storage.
drugClasses: Storage (beta-3 relaxes the detrusor, alpha-1 tightens the internal sphincter)
Overflow from a bladder that cannot empty

modules.title: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia
modules.description: A prostate that narrows the urethra two ways, by smooth-muscle tone and by bulk, and the two drug classes that each act on one of those.
drugClasses: Alpha-1 block together with 5-alpha reductase inhibition
